description: Generate one personalized outreach message per people-sheet row and save them as a new prospecting campaign. Takes the exact sheetId of a people sheet. Without rowIds, uses every people row in that sheet (up to 1000, added in batches of 25 within this one call). templateId must be the exact id of a saved template; otherwise the campaign is described inline with name, offering, goal and a concrete cta. goal is the campaign objective; conversion, with a concrete commercial next step in cta, fits a company that sells to businesses and has no campaigns yet. Every sheet column is used as labeled context. Campaign generation does not consume credits. The campaign is saved as a draft; nothing is sent. When people of the campaign still wait on their sheet row's e-mail, LinkedIn or phone lookup, enrichmentPending counts them by field and enrichmentPendingNote is a short sentence saying so; the address joins the campaign by itself when the lookup finishes.

acceptedCadenceCredits.description: Only on the second call: the cadenceCredits the first call returned (status needs_confirmation), after the person agreed.

businessContext.description: Company/product context used to ground the generated messages.

cadence.description: Optional cadence steps, in the same shape as a campaign cadence update, a step's variantB (version B for an A/B test) included and saved with the exact text given. Omit to generate later.

body.description: Message body for that step. Use {{firstName}}, {{company}}, {{headline}}, {{signal}} and {{senderFirstName}} when writing a campaign-wide template. {{outroDecisor}} is the first name of another decision maker at the person's own company (found by Nock, never invented), for a short follow-up such as 'Oi, {{firstName}}, isso é algo que você olharia ou fica mais com o {{outroDecisor}}?'; a person with none gets the sentence without a name ('...ou tem outra pessoa aí que cuida disso?') or the step's outroDecisorFallback. Leave empty only for a LinkedIn connection request without a note, and for linkedin_like.

branch.description: The path after the LinkedIn invite (only when the cadence has a LinkedIn message after the invite and e-mails or WhatsApp after it): accepted ("Aceitou o convite": the LinkedIn message first, then any steps for who accepted) or not_accepted ("Não aceitou em X dias": e-mails or WhatsApp for who did not accept; X is its first step's day minus the invite's, 1 to 21; never a LinkedIn step). Each person goes down one path. Steps on no path go first, then accepted, then not_accepted. Keep each step's branch as the campaign has it; a cadence sent without branches, with a LinkedIn message waiting for the accept before e-mails, gets the paths by itself.

channel.description: whatsapp_task is a WhatsApp step the person's sender sends from their own phone: a task on the WhatsApp screen, not sent by Nock, only for workspaces that have it (the save refuses it otherwise). linkedin_like is "Curtir post": Nock likes the newest LinkedIn post the person wrote from the campaign's LinkedIn account, a warm touch before the invite or a message; body empty, no subject; skipped when they posted nothing recent; to have the invite go some hours after the like, give the invite condition no_reply_hours (2 hours is the usual). linkedin_like is an opt-in step, only for workspaces that have it (the save refuses it otherwise)."Curtir post" likes only a post she wrote in recentDays (30 by default); with none it is skipped, unless commentFallback is true (off by default), when it likes her recent comment instead. like_post is an old name of it with commentFallback false. A linkedin_like step can do another interaction (interaction): like_comment (her recent comment, never on the post she was found on nor a watched competitor's), visit (a profile view she is told about) or reply_comment (a short public reply the Nock Agent writes from her comment, approved in the Inbox unless sending is automatic). No follow step exists.

commentFallback.description: linkedin_like "Curtir post" (no interaction or like) only: true likes her newest recent comment when she wrote no post in recentDays (never a comment on the post she was found on nor on a post of someone the campaign's signal watches); false (the default for a new step) skips the step then and the cadence goes on. The cadence read with the campaign shows each step's commentFallback as it goes out: keep it when the steps are sent back.

condition.description: What lets this step go after the one before. no_reply_days (the default): it goes on its day if there is no reply; no_reply_hours: it goes waitHours (1 to 72) after the step before was sent, if there is no reply, and its day is set from that step; invite_accepted: a LinkedIn message right after the invite, after the accept (automatic there); email_opened: only right after an e-mail step, it goes waitHours (default 24, min 1) after the person opens that e-mail and is skipped when it is not opened within fallbackDays (default 5). Opens are approximate (Apple Mail and security scanners). Omit to keep the step's current condition.

connectionCheck.description: Only on the cadence's first LinkedIn step: the node "Já é conexão?". invite: who is already a 1st-degree connection skips the invite and gets the first LinkedIn message right away; who is not gets the invite. message: the cadence starts with the LinkedIn message, no invite (a base of connections); who is not a connection gets no LinkedIn message, the other channels go on. A new cadence with LinkedIn gets invite when omitted; keep it as the campaign has it.

day.description: Day in the cadence (1–60). Omit to take the next free slot.

interaction.description: linkedin_like only: what the LinkedIn interaction does. like (default, "Curtir post"), like_comment, visit or reply_comment; see the channel's description. like_post is accepted as an old name of like with commentFallback false.

outroDecisorFallback.description: Only on a step whose text cites {{outroDecisor}}: the whole sentence that replaces the one citing it for a person whose company has no other decision maker found, e.g. 'Oi, {{firstName}}, isso é algo que você olharia ou tem outra pessoa aí que cuida disso?'. It may use {{firstName}} and {{company}}, never {{outroDecisor}}. Omit it to let Nock say it without a name.

ownPostsOnly.description: Old name, kept for compatibility: true is commentFallback false, false is commentFallback true. Use commentFallback.

recentDays.description: linkedin_like with like ("Curtir post"), like_comment or reply_comment only: how many days back a post or comment counts as recent (7 to 90; 30 for a new Curtir post and for like_comment, 14 for replies when omitted; a Curtir post saved before with none keeps 60).

subject.description: Email subject only. Omit for LinkedIn and WhatsApp.

taskDays.description: whatsapp_task only: days the task waits to be sent before the step is skipped (2 when omitted).

variantB.description: Version B of this step for an A/B test: each person gets version A (body) or version B, and the version with the higher reply rate becomes the step's only text once both went to enough people. Saved with the exact text given, never rewritten. subject only for e-mail steps (omitted: the e-mail keeps version A's subject). Not for a LinkedIn connection request nor a linkedin_like step. Saved on the campaign's template, never on one person's messages. A step sent without it has no version B.

constraints.description: Things the copy must never say or do.

cta.description: Desired next step: reply, book_call, accept_connect, share_resource, or custom text such as a demo or trial. Required and specific when goal is conversion.

give.description: Concrete value the sender can deliver before asking for the reader's time.

goal.description: Campaign objective: conversion, awareness, consultative, meeting, relationship, or custom text. conversion fits a workspace with no campaigns yet.

language.description: Defaults to the template language, or "Português (Brasil)".

name.description: Campaign name. Required unless the template supplies one.

offering.description: What the sender offers. Required unless the template supplies it.

rowIds.description: Optional. Exact row ids of that sheet. Omit to use every people row in the sheet (up to 1000).

senderCompany.description: Sender company name used in copy, same as REST senderCompany.

senderCompanyUrl.description: Sender company URL, same as REST senderCompanyUrl.

senderLinkChannels.description: Channels that may include the sender link: email, linkedin, whatsapp.

senderRole.description: Sender role used in copy, same as REST senderRole.

signalGate.description: How to use company buying signals: personalize messages, or skip people missing the chosen signal.

templateId.description: Only the exact id of a saved outreach template. Omit when name and offering are set.

tone.description: Message tone, e.g. consultative, professional, friendly, direct.

whatsappOnly.description: True for a campaign of WhatsApp only (the person picked WhatsApp alone): every step is a WhatsApp their sender sends from their own phone (tasks on the WhatsApp screen; Nock never sends it), no mailbox nor LinkedIn is needed, and only rows with a phone go in. Omit cadence to have it written. Only for workspaces that have the WhatsApp step.

whatsappStep.description: True adds one WhatsApp step near the end of the written cadence that the person's sender sends from their own phone (a task on the WhatsApp screen; Nock never sends it). Only for workspaces that have it; ignored otherwise.
